$$ \left|h^{u}(x)-h(x)\right|\leq\frac{L}{2}u^{2}\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\mathcal{Y}(u)}\left[\|y\|^{2}\right], $$

where the first inequality follows from the convexity and the second follows from the $L$ -smoothness of $h$ . We further notice that

$$ \mathbb{E}_{y\sim\mathcal{Y}(u}\left[\|y\|^{2}\right]=\frac{1}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\tilde{p}_{u}(\|y\|^{2})\,dy}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\|y\|^{2}\,\tilde{p}_{u}(\|y\|^{2})\,dy, $$

and since

$$ \displaystyle d\int_{0}^{+\infty}\tilde{p}_{u}(s^{2})s^{d-1}\,ds-\int_{0}^{+\infty}\tilde{p}_{u}(s^{2})s^{d+1}\,ds \displaystyle=\  \displaystyle\exp\!\left(-\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)\!\left(\frac{(\delta\underline{r}/u)^{d+2}}{d+2}-(\delta\underline{r}/u)^{d}\right)+2^{d/2}\!\left(\frac{d}{2}\gamma\!\left(\frac{d}{2},\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)\!-\gamma\!\left(1\!+\!\frac{d}{2},\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)\!\right) \displaystyle=\  \displaystyle\exp\!\left(-\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)\frac{(\delta\underline{r}/u)^{d+2}}{d+2}\geq 0 $$

(where we used $\gamma(s+1,x)=s\gamma(s,x)-x^{s}e^{-x}$ for the lower incomplete Gamma function $\gamma(s,x)$ ), we see that $\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\mathcal{Y}(u)}\left[\|y\|^{2}\right]\leq d$ , and therefore $|h^{u}(x)-h(x)|\leq\mathord{\raise 0.49991pt\hbox{$\displaystyle\genfrac{}{}{0.4pt}{}{1}{2}$}}u^{2}Ld$ . We also have

$$ \left|h^{u}(x)-h(x)\right|\leq\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\mathcal{Y}(u)}[|h(x+uy)-h(x)|]\leq uG\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\mathcal{Y}(u)}[\|y\|]\leq uG\sqrt{d}. $$

Finally, for the quantity $\kappa(u)$ , it’s straightforward to see that $\kappa(u)\leq 1$ , and we proceed to derive a lower bound on $\kappa(u)$ . Let $\beta=u^{-1}\delta\underline{r}/\sqrt{d}$ , and we have

$$ 1-\kappa(u)=\frac{\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^{d/2-1}\left(\beta e^{-\beta^{2}/2}\right)^{d}+\Gamma\!\left(\frac{d}{2},\beta^{2}\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}. $$

Noticing that

$$ \frac{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{d}{2},\beta^{2}\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}=\mathbb{P}_{z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})}\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}z_{i}^{2}\geq\beta^{2}d\right), $$

By (24) and Stirling’s formula $\Gamma\!\left(d/2\right)\geq\sqrt{2\pi}\left(d/2\right)^{\frac{d-1}{2}}e^{-d/2}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle 1-\kappa(u)\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi d}}\left(\beta e^{-(\beta^{2}-1)/2}\right)^{d}+\left(\beta^{2}e^{1-\beta^{2}}\right)^{d/2}\leq 1/200. $$

when $d\geq 2$ and $\beta=u^{-1}\delta\underline{r}/\sqrt{d}\geq 3$ . We then get

$$ \left\|\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{Z}(x,u)}\!\left[\mathsf{G}_{h}(x;u,z)\right]-\kappa(u)\nabla h^{u}(x)\right\|\leq\frac{2G\overline{R}}{u}\exp\!\left(\frac{d}{2}-\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{4u^{2}}\right), $$

and $\kappa(u)\geq 199/200$ when $\delta\underline{r}\geq 3u\sqrt{d}$ .

## Appendix B Proof of Lemma 3

We first provide some lemmas that will be used for subsequent analysis.

#### Lemma 11 (Concentration inequality (Boucheron et al., 2013, Theorem 5.6)).

Let $h:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be $G$ -Lipschitz. Then we have

$$ \mathbb{P}_{z}\!\left(|h(z)-\mathbb{E}_{z}[h(z)]|\geq t\right)\leq 2\exp\left(-t^{2}/(2G^{2})\right), $$

where $z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})$ .

With the help of the concentration inequality, we can prove the following lemma.

#### Lemma 12.

Let $h:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be $G$ -Lipschitz. Then

$$ \mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[\left|\frac{h(z)-h(-z)}{2}z_{i}\right|^{2}\right]\leq 12G^{2},\quad z=(z_{1},\ldots,z_{d})\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d}). $$

#### Proof.

Proof. The proof follows Shamir (2017, Lemmas 9 & 10) closely. Denote $\bar{h}=\mathbb{E}_{z}[h(z)]$ . We have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[\left|\frac{h(z)-h(-z)}{2}z_{i}\right|^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[z_{i}^{2}(h(z)-h(-z))^{2}\right]=\frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[z_{i}^{2}\left((h(z)-\bar{h})-(h(-z)-\bar{h})\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[z_{i}^{2}\left((h(z)-\bar{h})^{2}+(h(-z)-\bar{h})^{2}\right)\right]=\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[z_{i}^{2}(h(z)-\bar{h})^{2}\right]. $$

Then

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[z_{i}^{2}(h(z)\!-\!\bar{h})^{2}\right]\leq \displaystyle\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{z}[z_{i}^{4}]}\cdot\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{z}[(h(z)\!-\!\bar{h})^{4}]}=3\left(\int_{0}^{+\infty}\!\!\mathbb{P}_{z}\!\left((h(z)\!-\!\bar{h})^{4}\geq t\right)dt\right)^{\!1/2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle 3\left(\int_{0}^{+\infty}2\exp\left(-\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2G^{2}}\right)\,dt\right)^{1/2}=12G^{2}, $$

where we used Lemma 11 in the third step. ∎∎

We then derive bounds on the second moment of the gradient estimator (3) with $z\sim\mathcal{Z}(x,u)$ .

#### Lemma 13.

Let $h:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be $G$ -Lipschitz, and let $\delta\in(0,1)$ be arbitrary. Then for any $x\in(1-\delta)\mathcal{X}$ and any $i=1,\ldots,d$ ,

$$ \mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{Z}(x,u)}\!\left[\left\|\frac{h(x\!+\!uz)-h(x\!-\!uz)}{2u}z^{i}\right\|^{2}\right]\leq 12G^{2}d_{i}. $$

#### Proof.

Proof. Define the auxiliary function $\tilde{h}(z)=h\!\left(x+u\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}(x,u)}[z]\right),\forall z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . We then have

$$ \displaystyle\left|\tilde{h}(z_{1})-\tilde{h}(z_{2})\right|= \displaystyle\left|h\!\left(x+u\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}(x,u)}[z_{1}]\right)-h\!\left(x+u\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}(x,u)}[z_{2}]\right)\right| \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle uG\left\|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}(x,u)}[z_{1}]-\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}(x,u)}[z_{2}]\right\|\leq uG\left\|z_{1}-z_{2}\right\|, $$

showing that $\tilde{h}$ is a $uG$ -Lipschitz continuous function on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Moreover, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{Z}(x,u)}\!\left[\left\|(h(x+uz)-h(x-uz))z^{i}\right\|^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})}\!\left[\left\|(\tilde{h}(z)-\tilde{h}(-z))\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}_{i}(x^{i},u)}[z^{i}]\right\|^{2}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})}\!\left[\left\|(\tilde{h}(z)-\tilde{h}(-z))z^{i}\right\|^{2}\right], $$

where the last inequality follows from $\|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}_{i}(x^{i},u)}[z^{i}]\|\leq\|z^{i}\|$ as $\mathcal{S}_{i}(x^{i},u)$ is a convex set containing the origin.

Then by Lemma 12, we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})}\!\left[\left\|\frac{\tilde{h}(z)-\tilde{h}(-z)}{2u}z^{i}\right\|^{2}\right]\leq\frac{1}{u^{2}}\cdot 12u^{2}G^{2}\cdot d_{i}=12G^{2}d_{i}, $$

which gives the desired bound. ∎∎

We are now ready to prove (3). Recall that $\varepsilon^{+}_{j}(t)$ and $\varepsilon^{-}_{j}(t)$ are the independent additive noise on the observed local cost values. Denoting $\varepsilon_{j}(t)=\varepsilon^{+}_{j}(t)+\varepsilon^{-}_{j}(t)$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\big\|D_{j}(t)\,z^{i}(t)\big\|^{2}\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\frac{f_{j}(x(t)\!+\!uz(t))-f_{j}(x(t)\!-\!uz(t))}{2u}z^{i}(t)\right\|^{2}\bigg|\mathcal{F}_{t}\right]+\frac{1}{4u^{2}}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\varepsilon_{j}(t)^{2}\|z^{i}(t)\|^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{t}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle 12G^{2}d_{i}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}d_{i}, $$

where we used Lemma 13, the independence between $\varepsilon_{j}(t)$ and $z^{i}(t)$ , and the fact that $\mathbb{E}_{z^{i}\sim\mathcal{Z}^{i}(x,u)}\!\left[\|z^{i}\|^{2}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}_{z^{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d_{i}})}\!\left[\|z^{i}\|^{2}\right]\leq d_{i}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|G^{i}(t)\|^{2}\right]\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\|^{2}\right]\leq\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)d_{i}, $$

and by summing over $i=1,\ldots,n$ , we get the bound on $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|G(t)\|^{2}\right]$ .

## Appendix C Proof of Lemma 6

For each $\tau\geq 0$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left.\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\kappa(u)\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(\tau)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau)\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau} \displaystyle+\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\mathbb{E}\!\left[D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]-\kappa(u)\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(\tau)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau)\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}, $$

where the second term can be bounded by Lemma 2 and $\sum_{i=1}^{n}\overline{R}_{i}\leq\sqrt{n}\overline{R}$ as

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\mathbb{E}\!\left[D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]-\kappa(u)\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(\tau)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau)\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\frac{2G\overline{R}}{u}\exp\!\left(\frac{d}{2}\!-\!\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{4u^{2}}\right)\overline{R}_{i}\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\leq\frac{2G\overline{R}}{u}\exp\!\left(\frac{d}{2}\!-\!\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{4u^{2}}\right)\sqrt{n}\cdot\overline{R}\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}. $$

Therefore

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{\tau}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left.\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{\kappa(u)}{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\right]+\frac{2G\overline{R}}{u}\exp\!\left(\frac{d}{2}-\frac{\delta^{2}\underline{r}^{2}}{4u^{2}}\right)\sqrt{n}\cdot\overline{R}. $$

Now,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle \displaystyle=\  \displaystyle\left\langle\nabla f^{u}(x(t)),\tilde{x}-x(t)\right\rangle+\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(t)),x^{i}(t)-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle \displaystyle+\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(t)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle, $$

where $f^{u}(x)\coloneqq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j}f^{u}_{j}(x)$ . Note that by (17), we have $f^{u}(x)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\mathcal{Y}(u)}[f(x+uy)]$ , and together with the convexity of $f$ , we see that $f^{u}$ is convex and $f^{u}(x)\geq f(x)$ . Then by Lemma 2,

$$ \langle\nabla f^{u}(x(t)),\tilde{x}-x(t)\rangle\leq f^{u}(\tilde{x})-f^{u}(x(t))\leq f(\tilde{x})-f(x(t))+\min\!\left\{uG\sqrt{d},\frac{1}{2}u^{2}Ld\right\}, $$

and by Lemma 4, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(t)),x^{i}(t)-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle\leq\  \displaystyle\frac{1}{2n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left(2\sqrt{3}\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}\sqrt{d}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\!\|\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(t))\|^{2}\right]+\frac{\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|x^{i}(t)-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\|^{2}\right]}{2\sqrt{3}\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}\sqrt{d}}\right) \displaystyle\leq\  \displaystyle\frac{1}{2n}\left(2\sqrt{3}\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}\sqrt{d}\,nG^{2}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}\sqrt{d}}\,\eta^{2}\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)\cdot\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}(b_{ij}+\Delta)^{2}d_{i}\right) \displaystyle=\  \displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\left(2\sqrt{3}\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}G^{2}\sqrt{d}+2\sqrt{3}\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}\left(G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{24u^{2}}\right)\sqrt{d}\right)\leq 2\sqrt{3}\cdot\eta\bar{\mathfrak{b}}\left(G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{24u^{2}}\right)\sqrt{d}, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(t)),\tilde{x}^{i}-x^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle\leq\  \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}(x(t))\right\|\overline{R}_{i}\right]\leq\frac{L}{n}\!\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\!\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left[\|x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))-x(t)\|^{2}\right]}\cdot\overline{R}_{i} \displaystyle\leq\  \displaystyle\frac{\eta L\sqrt{d}}{n}\sqrt{12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}(b_{ij}+\Delta)\overline{R}_{i}\leq\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{nd}\sqrt{12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}}\cdot\overline{R}, $$

where the last step follows from Cauchy’s inequality. Summarizing these results, we get the desired bound.

## Appendix D Proof of Lemma 8

We have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[-\frac{1}{n}\!\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\!\left\langle\nabla^{i}f(x(t))-\nabla^{i}f(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))),D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{2n}\cdot\frac{1}{\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{n}}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\nabla^{i}f(x(t))-\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\|^{2}\right] \displaystyle+\frac{1}{2n}\cdot\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\|^{2}\right], $$

where we used the fact that $2\langle u,v\rangle\leq\|u\|^{2}/\epsilon+\epsilon\|v\|^{2}$ for any $\epsilon>0$ and any vectors $u,v$ . Now for the first term, we have

$$ \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|\nabla^{i}f(x(t))-\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\|^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\eta^{2}L^{2}d\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}(b_{ij}+\Delta)^{2}=\eta^{2}L^{2}n^{2}\bar{b}^{2}d\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right), $$

where we used Lemma 4 and the $L$ -smoothness of $f$ . And for the second term, we notice that

$$ \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(\tau))\big)\right\|^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum\nolimits_{\tau}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left.\left\|D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(\tau))\big)\right\|^{2}\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum\nolimits_{\tau}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left.\left\|D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)-\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau)\big)\right\|^{2}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\right], $$

and since $\mathbb{E}\!\left[D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]=\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}(x(\tau))$ for $\tau\geq 0$ by Lemma 1, we have

$$ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left.\left\|D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)-\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau)\big)\right\|^{2}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left.\left\|D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)\right\|^{2}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]\leq\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)d_{i}, $$

and consequently,

$$ \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))-\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(\tau))\big)\right\|^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)d_{i}\cdot\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum\nolimits_{\tau}\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\right]=n\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)d, $$

where we used Lemma 3 and the fact that $\tau^{i}_{j}(t)\geq 0$ when $t\geq B$ . Summarizing the above results gives the desired bound.

## Appendix E Proof of Lemma 9

By Lemma 1, for any $\tau\geq 0$ ,

$$ \mathbb{E}\bigg[\!-\!\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau)\big),D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\Big|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\bigg]=-\left\langle\nabla^{i}f(x(\tau)),\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}(x(\tau))\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}. $$

Then since $\tau^{i}_{j}(t)\geq 0$ when $t\geq B$ , we see that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[-\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big),D_{j}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))z^{i}(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\sum\nolimits_{\tau}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left.-\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau)\big),D_{j}(\tau)z^{i}(\tau)\right\rangle\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\right|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}\right]\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[-\sum\nolimits_{\tau}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f(x(\tau)),\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau)\big)\right\rangle\cdot\mathsf{1}_{\tau^{i}_{j}(t)=\tau}\bigg] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[-\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big),\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\rangle\right]. $$

We then notice that

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big),\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\rangle \displaystyle-\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f(x(t))-\nabla^{i}f(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))),\nabla^{i}f_{j}^{u}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)\right\rangle \displaystyle= \displaystyle-\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(t)\big),\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)-\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(t)\big)\right\rangle \displaystyle-\left\langle\nabla f(x(t)),\nabla f^{u}(x(t))-\nabla f(x(t))\right\rangle-\|\nabla f(x(t))\|^{2}. $$

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[-\frac{1}{n}\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\left\langle\nabla^{i}f\big(x(t)\big),\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)-\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(t)\big)\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{2n}\!\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}\!\mathbb{E}\!\left[2\sqrt{3}\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{nd}\left\|\nabla^{i}f(x(t))\right\|^{2}+\frac{\left\|\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(\tau^{i}_{j}(t))\big)-\nabla^{i}f^{u}_{j}\big(x(t)\big)\right\|^{2}}{2\sqrt{3}\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{nd}}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\left(2\sqrt{3}\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{nd}G^{2}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}\eta L\bar{b}n^{3/2}\sqrt{d}}\eta^{2}L^{2}\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right)d\cdot\sum\nolimits_{i,j=1}^{n}(b_{ij}+\Delta)^{2}\right) \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{\eta L\bar{b}\sqrt{nd}}{2\sqrt{3}}\left(12G^{2}+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2u^{2}}\right), $$

where we used Lemma 4 and the $L$ -smoothness of $f_{j}^{u}$ , and

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[-\left\langle\nabla f(x(t)),\nabla f^{u}(x(t))-\nabla f(x(t))\right\rangle\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{3}\left\|\nabla f(x(t))\right\|^{2}+3\left\|\nabla f^{u}(x(t))-\nabla f(x(t))\right\|^{2}\right]\leq\frac{1}{6}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\nabla f(x(t))\|^{2}\right]+\frac{3}{2}u^{2}L^{2}d, $$

where we used Lemma 1. Summarizing these bounds completes the proof.
